cover.title: Your Medical Bills Have a Cap

lines.text: Most health plans legally can't make you pay over $12,000.
lines.say: Most health plans legally can't make you pay over twelve grand.

lines.text: In 2027, that cap is $12,000 for one person's covered in-network care. In 2026, it's $10,600.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-seven, that cap is twelve thousand dollars for one person's covered in-network care. In twenty twenty-six, it's ten thousand six hundred dollars.

scene.label: 2027 legal out-of-pocket cap, one person
scene.sub: HHS/CMS limit, in-network care, most plans ($10,600 in 2026)

lines.say: Back in twenty fourteen, it was six thousand three hundred fifty dollars.

lines.text: The cap works with two other numbers. The premium is what you pay every month just to have the plan.
lines.say: The cap works with two other numbers. The premium is what you pay every month just to have the plan.

lines.text: The deductible is what you pay for care before the plan starts to help.
lines.say: The deductible is what you pay for care before the plan starts to help.

lines.text: The out-of-pocket max is the ceiling. After it, covered in-network care is paid 100%.
lines.say: And the out-of-pocket max is the ceiling. After that, covered in-network care is paid in full.

lines.text: Take a $30,000 bill. A $2,000 deductible plus 20% of the rest is $7,600.
lines.say: Take a thirty thousand dollar bill. A two thousand dollar deductible plus twenty percent of the rest is seven thousand six hundred.

lines.text: But with a $6,000 max, you stop paying at $6,000.
lines.say: But with a six thousand dollar max, you stop paying at six thousand.

lines.text: The catch? Premiums never count toward the cap. Most out-of-network care doesn't either.
lines.say: The catch? Premiums never count toward the cap, and most out-of-network care doesn't either.

lines.text: So for covered in-network care, your worst case is a year of premiums plus the out-of-pocket max.
lines.say: So for covered in-network care, your worst case is a year of premiums, plus the out-of-pocket max.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Most health plans can't make you pay over $12,000
post.ig:
Most health plans legally can't make you pay over $12,000.
That's the 2027 out-of-pocket cap for one person's covered in-network care, up from $10,600 in 2026 and $6,350 in 2014.
Premium: what you pay every month to have the plan. Deductible: what you pay before the plan starts to help. Out-of-pocket max: the ceiling.
Premiums never count toward the cap, and most out-of-network care doesn't either.
Sources: HealthCare.gov, HHS/CMS.
